text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT — increased 5xx and timeouts observed for runtime-service (us-west-2) after canary deploy at 20:12 UTC. p95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s, p99 from 350ms -> 6.2s, error rate ~2.6% (was 0.03%). paging oncall @alice_nguyen :rotating_light:

alice_nguyen: seeing it in the dashboard now. canary-1 rolled ~20:10. grabbing traces + logs. can someone post the deploy id?

jorge_ramirez: @alice_nguyen deploy id is deploy-2026-03-15-6681 (canary-1). I pushed a tiny refactor to request multiplexing in the runtime loop — suspicious but not certain.

maya_lin: adding telemetry: `curl "https://telemetry.internal/prod/runtime-service/metrics?window=5m"` shows KV cache hit rate dropped 30% around the same time. maybe cache warming issue?

sam_mueller: Observability: https://grafana.internal/d/runtime-service?orgId=1 (short link). top traces show time spent in `batch_executor.py` waiting on connection/queue. also 502 spikes at the gateway level.

observability-bot: Alert details: alert_id=A-89321, rule=p99_latency_us_west, threshold=5s, triggered=20:15 UTC. Top endpoints: /v1/complete, /v1/chat/stream.

alice_nguyen: quick triage checklist: 1) roll canary back? 2) scale up? 3) temporary routing (region failover)? 4) patch suspect code? Need decision.

jorge_ramirez: we should revert canary-1 to be safe. I can revert the PR but want to capture logs. any objections?

nina_clark: product — customer impact: internal usage telemetry shows ~8% of active tokens failing for realtime customers in us-west. escalation to CS in progress. We need ETA to mitigation for comms.

alice_nguyen: agreed roll back canary-1 now. @deploy-bot can you initiate rollback to image `runtime:2026-03-14-ff23` for us-west-2 canary group?

deploy-bot: Rollback started: rollback_job=rb-5157773333-1. initiating canary group revert -> previous image. ETA ~ 90s. Will post status updates.

maya_lin: while rollback runs, do not restart any runtime pods in us-west. also disabling new multiplex config via ff for canary group (temp).

jorge_ramirez: logs captured: devx://logs/runtime/canary-1/20:12-20:20 — core stack traces show `batch_executor` blocked on `asyncio.wait_for(..., timeout=0.05)` getting cancelled. suspect batching change introduced a race during high concurrency.

alice_nguyen: deploy-bot status?

deploy-bot: Rollback complete for canary-1 at 20:18 UTC. All canary nodes are running `runtime:2026-03-14-ff23`. health checks passing.

observability-bot: Metrics update: p95 back to ~140ms within 90s post-rollback, p99 trending down, error rate back to 0.05% after 2m. Gateway 502s reduced substantially.

nina_clark: confirmed with CS — customer-impact window ~20:12–20:18 UTC. initiating outbound comms draft.

sam_mueller: follow-up actions: - revert PR fully and open a revert-PR, - add extra e2e canary load tests to the CI profile, - add guardrail to batching config to prevent negative backpressure (e.g., min_batch_wait_ms). I'll open tickets.

jorge_ramirez: I'm preparing a fix branch that avoids the new wait_for pattern and adds safer cancellation semantics. will run it in a staging soak.

alice_nguyen: incident severity: Sev2 (customer-visible but mitigated rapidly). creating incident record. notes: fast rollback effective mitigation; root cause likely batching race + cache-warm interplay.

observability-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-2154. linked alerts: A-89321, A-89322.

nina_clark: Customer comms: short note drafted — will send to CS for review: "We detected increased errors/timeouts impacting real-time inference in us-west-2 between 20:12–20:18 UTC due to a canary deploy. We reverted the canary and services have recovered. No long-term data loss. We're investigating root cause and will follow up"

maya_lin: temporary mitigations to reduce blast radius if similar happens: - disable canary multiplexing flag by default, - increase initial cache prober concurrency during rollout, - add p95/p99 smoke tests to preflight job.

sam_mueller: I'm taking the oncall handoff for the night rotation at 21:00 UTC. if anything re-triggers, page me on mobile. next steps: 1) Jorge to validate fix in staging, 2) SRE to add load smoke checks to deploy pipeline, 3) Dev to open revert PR and postmortem draft.

jorge_ramirez: ack — will push staging PR and ping here with results. expected earliest PR in 2–3 hours.

alice_nguyen: thanks team. closing active pager and marking incident as mitigated. handoff notes: see INC-2026-2154 for timeline, links to logs and traces, and list of affected customers.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation acknowledged by alice_nguyen at 20:22 UTC. severity downgraded.

sam_mueller: (post-handoff) I'll own the postmortem. please drop any logs/snippets in INC-2026-2154 thread. add any follow-ups to the incident checklist: - deploy gating for batching changes, - automated canary perf regression test, - customer comms follow-up in 24hrs.

nina_clark: thanks all. CS will send the message in 30m and will attach the timeline. :white_check_mark:

alice_nguyen: re-open if anything recurs. good work. :thumbsup:
